Lessons.Title: Create Scaled Picture Graphs
ExplanationParagraphs: Grade 3 Unit 1 Lesson 4 of Illustrative Mathematics K–5 first edition (2021) asks learners to represent REAL class data using a scaled picture graph. The learning goal is to build a graph where one whole picture represents TWO students; a HALF picture can represent ONE student. No survey quantities are fixed by the publisher and classroom evidence requires teacher review.

Original 2021 warm-up: THREE groups of FIVE dots (15) and FIVE groups of FIVE dots (25), 30 seconds quiet thinking and one minute partner discussion for each display. Use original Edulytics-authored dot illustrations instead of copyright-restricted publisher image bytes.

Activity 1 — Ways to Travel (15 minutes). Students survey classmates in groups of four and record one response per pupil in a teacher-controlled paper table before class totals are calculated. The six original options are car (C), train (T), boat (B), balloon (Bal), plane (P) and helicopter (H). Discuss advantages and limits of a raw list versus grouped category totals. The student companion collects only six aggregate numeric counts and survey provenance notes; it must NOT store classmates' names or pretend an entered count proves the survey took place. At the first Math Community reflection, the teacher records norms used when collecting data.

Activity 2 — Create a Scaled Picture Graph (20 minutes). Use those exact authentic totals to make a graph with title, category labels and the key ONE WHOLE SYMBOL = TWO STUDENTS. If a count is odd, represent the final learner by half of the chosen symbol; do not round that learner away. The original Student Facing task includes a blank drawing grid and a partner comparison. The teacher can offer physical cubes in groups of two for accessibility and supports partner statements with MLR8 prompts; neither manipulatives nor teacher assessment is numerically auto-certified.

Lesson synthesis (10 minutes) BEFORE Cool-down: revisit the actual class scaled picture graph. Ask separately: (1) if TWO more chose Balloon, add ONE full symbol; (2) if ONE more chose Car, add a HALF symbol when old count was even, or complete an existing half to a whole symbol when old count was odd. Discuss the Math Community norms that supported collaboration and revise as needed. The source teacher-guide Cool-down asks pupils to add the travel preferences of FOUR absent Plane learners to the source scaled picture graph, which requires TWO new full symbols under key 2. The first-party five-minute Cool-down shows a fictional Edulytics graph rather than publisher artwork, grades the two-symbol source mathematical transfer, and requires teacher review of the student drawing. Other independent Edulytics numeric checks are optional and do not count as source Cool-down.

KeyConcepts.Title: Teacher-led survey provenance
KeyConcepts.Definition: The values represent one actual answer per learner gathered in the current class.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use one response per person and count the six original categories accurately; preserve the individual paper record privately and send only aggregates online.
KeyConcepts.Example: A blank classroom paper sheet records 'C', 'T', 'B', 'Bal', 'P' or 'H' for each pupil; it must not be misrepresented as completed before polling.

KeyConcepts.Title: Scale of 2
KeyConcepts.Definition: One whole picture in the graph stands for exactly two students.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Whole symbol count is floor(students ÷ 2). An odd leftover student requires exactly one half symbol.
KeyConcepts.Example: For a hypothetical 7 students choosing Boat, draw 3 whole pictures and 1 half picture, because 3 × 2 + 1 = 7.

KeyConcepts.Title: Synthesis — two more for Balloon
KeyConcepts.Definition: A change of two students under a two-to-one key adds one whole graph symbol.
KeyConcepts.Rule: When Balloon count rises by two, add one full mark to that category while keeping other category totals unchanged.
KeyConcepts.Example: If 4 pupils chose Balloon and 2 more hypothetically join, the graph changes from 2 whole marks to 3.

KeyConcepts.Title: Synthesis — one more for Car
KeyConcepts.Definition: A change of one student changes the fractional half-symbol representation.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For an even starting count, add a new half symbol; for an odd starting count, complete its existing half symbol into a whole.
KeyConcepts.Example: If Car starts with 5 students (2 whole + 1 half), one more gives 6 (3 whole), not 2 whole + 2 halves.

WorkedExamples.Title: Warm-up source 2021: groups of five
WorkedExamples.Question: Three groups of five and five groups of five: how many dots do you see?
WorkedExamples.Method: Skip-count by five; explain two arrangements to a partner.
Steps: Count 3 groups of 5.
Three fives equal 15.
Count 5 groups of 5.
Five fives equal 25.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 15 dots in one arrangement; 25 in the other.

WorkedExamples.Title: Activity 1 — tally real responses privately
WorkedExamples.Question: What must you collect before the class's six scaled picture-graph counts can be trusted?
WorkedExamples.Method: Create a paper list of one classmate preference per pupil, then produce only six anonymous counts.
Steps: Ask one classmate which original travel option they would like.
Record the response in the teacher-supervised paper list, once per pupil.
Tally all individual C/T/B/Bal/P/H responses into six numeric totals.
Ask the teacher to confirm the totals; do not upload names or invent missing responses.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Six teacher-checked class totals derived from a real individual-response list.
WorkedExamples.Check: The sum of the six totals equals the number of pupils who actually answered; teacher must confirm the paper provenance.

WorkedExamples.Title: Activity 2 — odd numbers and half pictures
WorkedExamples.Question: In a FICTIONAL example only, seven students prefer Boat. How can key two show seven exactly?
WorkedExamples.Method: Divide into pairs and one remaining single student.
Steps: Make three pairs from six of the seven pupils.
Draw three whole pictures, each worth two.
Represent the remaining pupil by a half picture worth one.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Three whole symbols and one half symbol.
WorkedExamples.Check: 3 × 2 + 1 = 7, with no rounding or invented real class values.

WorkedExamples.Title: Synthesis — Balloon plus two and Car plus one
WorkedExamples.Question: A graph uses key two. What if two more students choose Balloon? What if one more chooses Car?
WorkedExamples.Method: Treat these as two SEPARATE hypothetical graph-change questions on the real class survey.
Steps: For Balloon, a plus-two change always adds one whole picture.
For Car, inspect whether the existing number of students is even or odd.
If Car is even, add a half mark; if Car is odd, complete an existing half picture into a whole.
Explain both changes against the teacher's current graph rather than assuming either change actually occurred.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Balloon gains 1 whole mark; Car gains 1 half mark of value, either by adding a new half or completing the old half.
WorkedExamples.Check: One full picture represents 2; one half picture represents 1, so both hypothetical additions are exact.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original 2021 source Cool-down: four more Plane pupils
WorkedExamples.Question: A group of FOUR absent pupils also chooses Plane. How many additional whole pictures should be drawn in the Plane category on a graph with key one picture = two pupils?
WorkedExamples.Method: Represent the change, not a fabricated fixed initial source category count; teacher reviews the student's actual pictograph.
Steps: Identify the key: one full symbol represents two pupils.
Divide the four additional Plane pupils into pairs: 4 ÷ 2 = 2.
Draw TWO additional complete picture symbols in Plane without changing any other group.
For Edulytics fictional starting Plane value 3 only, the new total 7 appears as three full and one half symbols.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Add two new whole picture symbols in the Plane category.
WorkedExamples.Check: 2 additional full pictures × 2 pupils per picture = 4 additional Plane pupils.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Importing fixed counts from an earlier published graph as if they are current class survey responses.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 2021 L04 explicitly asks pupils to gather their classmates' own preferences.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep a teacher-supervised paper list, tally actual responses and label any illustrative dataset as fictional.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using only full symbols for an odd category count and rounding up or down.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: At scale 2, an odd count leaves one individual who must be represented accurately.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Draw floor(n/2) whole symbols and one half symbol for n mod 2 = 1.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating Balloon +2 and Car +1 as the same graph update.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Two students mean one whole symbol; one student changes the half-symbol parity.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Discuss each source synthesis question separately, considering whether Car already has an odd number.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming source task completion merely because six numeric totals were entered.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source also requires individual survey collection, teacher observation, a learner-drawn scaled graph, partner comparison and Maths Community norms.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher reviews the physical survey and drawing; typed totals and auto-grading do not replace those source activities.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Replacing the original Cool-down of four absent Plane pupils with an extra-two question.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The first-edition 2021 Teacher Guide source Cool-down specifies four newly added Plane survey responses and exactly two additional pictures when each picture represents two.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep plus four as the required source task and teacher-scored drawing; plus two is optional Edulytics extension only.

SummaryPoints: 2021 warm-up: first display three groups of five = 15; second five groups of five = 25; partner mathematical explanations and first-party graphic.
15-minute activity: privately record ONE real preferred-travel response per classmate using C/T/B/Bal/P/H, then tally six categories without uploading names.
20-minute activity: draw exact scaled picture graph where a whole symbol = two students and a half symbol = one; include key, title, labels and discuss with partner.
Lesson synthesis BEFORE Cool-down: two more Balloon => one whole symbol; one more Car => half-symbol change or completing an existing half.

The 2021 Teacher Guide original Cool-down mathematically adds FOUR absent Plane pupils, so TWO additional full images at key two; the first-party source-aligned Cool-down requires teacher assessment of the drawing, not numeric scoring alone.
Original dot/balloon/grid images and the Student Task Statements PDF remain external unverified source-material boundaries; do not claim original-artwork parity.
